invariants.title: Regular-post at-most-once transaction and exact replay
invariants.statement: Before a regular-post X create request can be transmitted, one durable single-use attempt must bind the exact payload, selected quote/image identity, post-cycle histories and recovery delays. An uncertain attempt must survive restart as a global manual-reconciliation barrier whose ordinary-file identity and exact bytes remain stable across explicit file and parent-directory synchronisation. The restart-persistent successor-first protocol must itself be durably activated before any remote lane may open. A newly recorded ambiguity must create, synchronise and revalidate ambiguous_post_outcome.restart_barrier.json before linking the legacy marker name. An installation without the exact activation sentinel must fail closed across every process restart; a legacy-only marker must never be migrated by the running daemon and must be reconciled while stopped before clean offline activation. A process-local latch alone does not satisfy restart safety: either the inactive protocol, a successor or unresolved receipt must remain durably discoverable after marker disappearance, abrupt process death and every later restart, and either marker namespace entry, an unresolved receipt, protocol inactivity, or either process-local barrier must block every remote-write lane. A confirmed attempt must promote atomically to the established receipt, block unrelated remote writes while local schedule work remains pending, preserve the exact authoritative histories and future schedules, reconcile idempotently, and never cause a second remote post. The daemon must never retire the restart barrier; only the offline, instance-lock-bound reconciliation protocol may durably archive the exact barriers and reconciliation receipt and retire the successor as its final synchronised namespace transition. Clean protocol activation is a separate stopped, instance-lock-bound operation which refuses every active marker and unresolved receipt.
invariants.failure_if_violated: A hard process death after X accepts a post but before the first confirmed receipt can duplicate the post, or a later recovery can reconstruct different local cycle state from the state that followed the confirmed post.
invariants.status_rationale: The regular lane writes a strict, no-follow durable source receipt and revalidates its identity and bytes while publishing a payload/source/inode-bound journal and immutable fence. The final one-shot transport authority revalidates and consumes the journal/fence pair immediately before the exact POST /2/tweets transport. Within the cooperative single-instance, same-state-owner protocol, supported writers of reserved transaction names hold the same instance lock and serialize destructive transaction mutations within the owning process. A mutation already visible at a documented revalidation boundary refuses transport, while source loss after journal/fence publication leaves an independent durable restart barrier. Concurrent same-UID mutation inside a validation-to-pathname-syscall interval, or mutation of the state directory outside the lock protocol, is outside this guarantee. Malformed JSON, duplicate names, non-finite values and unsafe types fail closed. A valid response confirms the journal before confirmed-source lineage permits promotion and later history, schedule or retirement changes. Retirement validates the identity presented at every observed phase, is crash-visible and verifier-gated by the process-lifetime instance lock, and relies on cooperative exclusive namespace ownership for its final pathname unlink. Media upload uses a separate exact receipt/fence and can hand off only beneath an already prepared main-post journal/fence. The v2 protocol activation sentinel inventories these additional barriers and treats its v1 namespace as forbidden legacy state. Interrupted exchange staging and offline reconciliation states remain fail closed, but not every exact safe staging/archive state is automatically resumed.

verification.rationale: Tests use hard process exits at transaction, final-authority and receipt-retirement boundaries; delete or replace the source, journal and fence in fresh processes; reject duplicate/nonfinite/noncanonical receipt JSON and unsafe namespace types; and exercise same-byte post-bind ABA, verifier-gated mutation and confirmed-source lineage before protected state changes. Literal interpreters retain the successor-first and protocol-migration proofs, while media tests require a durable upload barrier beneath the prepared main-post transaction. Strict durable-proof tests distinguish an exact transaction object which may release retained SIGINT from a merely conservative inspection blocker which may not. Exact exchange staging and safe partial offline reconciliation remain fail closed but are not automatically completed, so verification remains partial.

validations.purpose: Exercise durable pre-send intent, hard-death ambiguity retention, exact bound schedule after-state, pending-schedule recovery, conservative post-transmission status handling and at-most-once restart behavior.

Interrupted offline reconciliation remains fail-closed, but the command does not automatically resume every safe partial archive state; an operator may need to inspect and rerun recovery.

invariants.title: Single process owns recovery and posting
invariants.statement: One process-lifetime instance lock must be acquired before receipt reconciliation, outbox recovery, scheduler mutation or remote-write preparation and must exclusively lock an opened state-directory inode. It must, without following symbolic links, bind one ordinary, single-link lock pathname to the acquired descriptor's device, inode, exact canonical owner record and exclusive open-file-description lock. A state-directory-device/inode-derived Linux abstract socket supplies an additional same-network-namespace singleton but is not the cross-namespace authority. Before every non-read remote operation, the designated descriptors must prove their own exclusive flock and OFD ownership, separate descriptors must prove exclusion on both the file and directory inode, the bound path identities must remain unchanged and the abstract singleton must remain bound. Every destructive journal, media or source-receipt mutation must additionally consume a narrow authority bound to the exact live instance-lock verifier, and that verifier must re-prove ownership on every use before any namespace inspection or mutation. The supported offline marker reconciler must acquire and continuously revalidate the identical directory-inode and file-lock namespace and therefore cannot run concurrently with the daemon across network namespaces, lock-file replacement or path aliases.
invariants.failure_if_violated: A followed, aliased, replaced or no-longer-owned lock pathname can create two lock namespaces or make an unlocked process look like the owner. The daemon and an offline reconciler or second process can then reconcile or post concurrently, race state files, and defeat otherwise correct receipt and ambiguity barriers.
invariants.status_rationale: The implementation opens and exclusively flocks the state-directory inode before any other ownership boundary. Linux inode-lock semantics make that lock common to path aliases and network namespaces; this host cannot create the second network namespace needed for a direct namespace test, so focused tests exercise the same-inode exclusion mechanism through path replacement and aliases. It binds a supplementary Linux abstract socket derived from the directory device/inode, opens the file lock relative to the held directory descriptor with no-follow semantics, requires one ordinary link, writes and reads back the exact canonical device/inode/PID identity, and holds both BSD flock and a Linux OFD write lock. Linux /proc/self/fdinfo, F_OFD_GETLK, independent exclusion probes, path identities and the supplementary socket are revalidated at remote boundaries. Destructive journal, media and exact source-retirement entry points reject callers before inspection unless they receive a narrow TransactionMutationAuthority issued from the daemon's exact verifier, and every authority use calls that verifier again. Historical-context mutation receives the same authority through its bound provider. The test bypass remains limited to explicit loopback endpoints. Bootstrap orders acquisition before recovery, one-shot commands share the guarded path, and the offline marker reconciler acquires all boundaries. Interrupted transaction and marker-reconciliation states preserve a blocking durable object but some legitimate staging/archive states still require deterministic operator inspection and rerun. The missing direct second-network-namespace regression and that automatic-resume liveness limitation keep the broader invariant partial.

Authority tests prove every destructive low-level entry point refuses before inspection without an authority, every use rechecks the bound verifier, the bot issues authority from the exact instance-lock verifier, and historical-context mutation refuses without its provider. Fresh-process retirement tests prove crash states preserve a barrier, but not automatic completion of every legitimate partial state. A second network namespace is not directly exercised.
